title: At work
description: Colleagues, meetings, schedules, emails and after-work dinners, polite and formal.

items.note: 안녕하십니까 is the 합니다체 form of 안녕하세요, the usual way to greet superiors at work.
distractors: Goodbye, director.
Thank you, director.
Nice to meet you, director.

items.english: to work hard, to take trouble
Thank you for your hard work.
items.note: Said when a task or the workday ends. It is safe to use with superiors too.
distractors: Please keep working hard.
Sorry for the trouble.
Good luck with your work.

good.english: You too, thanks for your work.

items.note: Said to someone still working as you leave. Many avoid it with superiors.
distractors: Thank you for your hard work.
Take care on the way home.
Please help me with this.

items.note: The polite way to leave before colleagues or your boss. 들어가다 here means going home.
distractors: I'll go into the office first.
I'll be leaving a little late.
Please go home before me.

good.english: Okay, thanks for your hard work.

bad.english: Get off at the next station.

items.korean: 먼저 가세요, 저는 이거만 끝내고 갈게요.
items.english: Go ahead, I'll leave once I finish this.
distractors: Go ahead, I've already finished this.
Wait for me, I'll finish this quickly.
Go ahead, I'll start this tomorrow.

items.korean: 저는 이번에 새로 들어온 신입 사원입니다.
items.english: I'm the new employee who just joined.
distractors: I'm the employee who is leaving this time.
I'm the new manager who just joined.
I'm the new student who just enrolled.

good.english: Oh, I've heard a lot about you.

items.english: I start working on this team today.
distractors: I stopped working on this team today.
I worked on this team until today.
I'll join this team tomorrow.

items.english: from now on, in the future
I look forward to working with you.
items.note: Lit. 'I humbly ask you to treat me well.' The standard close of a self-introduction.
distractors: Thank you for all your help.
Please take good care of yourself.
I hope we meet again.

good.english: Likewise, I look forward to it.

items.english: Let me introduce our new colleague.
distractors: Let me introduce our new boss.
Our new colleague will introduce himself.
Let me introduce an old friend.
Where do you work now?
Where will you work next?
How long did you work there?

good.english: I worked at a bank before.
I worked at a small company for three years.

items.english: If you have any questions, ask me anytime.
distractors: If you have questions, ask the team leader.
Ask me anything after the meeting.
If you're curious, look it up yourself.

good.english: Thank you, I'll learn a lot.

items.korean: 이 회사에서 일한 지 얼마나 됐어요?
items.english: How long have you worked at this company?
distractors: How far is this company from here?
How many people work at this company?
How long will you work at this company?

items.note: Use the title instead of a name or 'you': 팀장님 의견, not 당신 의견.
distractors: What's your schedule, team leader?
How are you feeling, team leader?
What did the director say, team leader?

items.english: What is the new team leader like?
distractors: Who is the new team leader?
When does the new team leader start?
What was the old team leader like?

items.english: Do you have a moment, assistant manager?
items.note: Titles replace names at work: 대리님 or 김 대리님. 씨 is only for peers or juniors.
distractors: What time is it, assistant manager?
Are you feeling okay, assistant manager?
Are you free tonight, assistant manager?

good.english: I'm a bit busy now, is later okay?

items.english: Could you help me with this?
distractors: Can I help you with this?
Could you do this for me tomorrow?
Could you explain this to me?

good.english: Of course, what do you need?

items.english: The section chief isn't at his desk right now.
items.note: Titles rise 사원, 대리, 과장, 차장, 부장; add 님 when addressing them.
distractors: The section chief is at his desk right now.
The section chief has gone home for the day.
The section chief is in a meeting right now.
Would you write the report for me?
Did you read my report?
Could you print the report?

good.english: Sure, I'll look at it today.
Send it to me by email now.

items.english: I read your report. Nice work.
distractors: I haven't read your report yet.
Please rewrite your report.
I wrote the report, please read it.

items.english: I just sent you an email.
distractors: I'll send you an email later.
I just got your email.
I forgot to send the email.
Did you send my email?
Did you get my text?
Can you check my report?

items.english: I'll send the materials as an attachment.
distractors: I'll print the materials for you.
Please send me the attached file.
The attached file didn't open.

items.korean: 이 부분만 수정해서 다시 보내 주세요.
items.english: Please fix just this part and send it again.
distractors: Please delete this part and send it again.
Please check this part and call me.
I fixed this part and sent it again.

good.english: Okay, I'll fix it right away.

items.english: I'll submit the report by tomorrow morning.
distractors: I submitted the report this morning.
I'll submit the report by tomorrow evening.
Please submit the report by tomorrow morning.
Is the deadline today?
Can we move the deadline?
Who set the deadline?

items.english: Please send it by this Friday.
distractors: Please send it after this Friday.
Please send it by next Friday.
I'll send it this Friday.

items.korean: 마감을 다음 주로 미룰 수 있을까요?
items.english: Could we push the deadline to next week?
distractors: Could we move the deadline up to this week?
Is the deadline next week?
Could we cancel next week's meeting?

items.english: to work late, to do overtime
The deadline is tomorrow, so I have to work late today.
distractors: The deadline was yesterday, so I stayed late.
The deadline is tomorrow, so I'm leaving early.
The deadline is today, so I have to work late tomorrow.

good.english: Me too, let's have dinner together.

items.korean: 다음 주 일정 좀 알려 주세요.
items.english: Please let me know next week's schedule.
distractors: Please tell me this week's schedule.
Please change next week's schedule.
I'll let you know next week's schedule.

items.korean: 다음 주 월요일부터 부산으로 출장 가요.
items.english: I'm going to Busan on a business trip from next Monday.
distractors: I'm coming back from a business trip to Busan next Monday.
I'm going on vacation to Busan next Monday.
I went to Busan on a business trip last Monday.

good.english: How many days will you be gone?

items.english: Are you free on Friday afternoon?
distractors: Are you free on Friday morning?
Were you free on Friday afternoon?
Are you busy this afternoon?

items.english: I'll check my schedule and let you know.
distractors: I checked my schedule and told you.
Please check your schedule and tell me.
I'll check the email and let you know.

items.english: What time does the meeting start?
distractors: What time does the meeting end?
Where is the meeting held?
How long is the meeting?

items.english: The meeting is in the big meeting room.
distractors: The meeting is in the small meeting room.
The meeting was in the big meeting room.
The big meeting room is booked.

items.english: Well then, let's begin the meeting.
distractors: Well then, let's end the meeting.
The meeting will start late.
Well then, let's take a break.

items.english: We've moved today's meeting to tomorrow morning.
distractors: We've moved tomorrow's meeting to today.
Today's meeting has been cancelled.
We've moved today's meeting to tomorrow afternoon.

good.english: What time was it moved to?

bad.english: Yes, this is the right bus.

distractors: Did you attend yesterday's meeting?
Can you lead tomorrow's meeting?
Can you book a room for tomorrow's meeting?
Did your presentation go well?
When is your presentation?
Who is giving the presentation?

good.english: Not yet, I'll finish it tonight.

items.english: If you have any questions, please let me know.
distractors: If you have questions, please write them down.
Please answer the questions.
If you have any questions, ask me later.

items.english: Let's wrap up today's meeting here.
distractors: Today's meeting will be held here.
Let's start today's meeting here.
Today's meeting has been moved.

good.english: Thank you for your hard work.

items.english: to break down, to be out of order

distractors: The copier is working again.
The printer is out of paper.
The computer is broken.

items.korean: 죄송합니다, 차가 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같습니다.
items.english: I'm sorry, traffic is bad, so I'll be a little late.
items.note: Call or message before the start time; lateness is taken seriously in Korean offices.
distractors: I'm sorry, traffic was bad, so I was a little late.
I'm sorry, the subway stopped, so I'll be late.
I'm sorry, the car broke down, so I can't come.

good.korean: 괜찮아요, 회의는 십 분 후에 시작해요.
good.english: It's fine, the meeting starts in ten minutes.

bad.english: Yes, get off at the next station.

items.english: I overslept and I'm late. I'm sorry.
distractors: I overslept, but I wasn't late.
I stayed up late, so I'm tired.
I'm sorry, I'll be late tomorrow.

items.korean: 몸이 안 좋아서 오늘 쉬어도 될까요?
items.english: I'm not feeling well. Could I take today off?
distractors: I'm not feeling well. Could I leave early today?
I'm feeling better, so I'll come in today.
My family is sick, so could I work from home?

good.english: Of course, get plenty of rest.
Make sure you see a doctor.

bad.english: This food is good for you.

items.english: I've caught a cold. May I leave early today?
items.note: 조퇴 is leaving work or school early, usually because you are ill.
distractors: I've caught a cold. May I stay home today?
I'm over my cold. May I stay late today?
My child has a cold. May I come in late today?

good.english: Sure, go home and rest well.
Take some medicine and sleep early.

bad.english: Okay, I'll put it in a bag.

items.korean: 다음 주 금요일에 연차 써도 될까요?
items.english: Could I take a day of leave next Friday?
items.note: 연차 is paid annual leave, used a day at a time; 반차 is half a day. You 'use' it: 연차를 쓰다.
distractors: Could I take this Friday off?
Could I work next Friday instead?
Could I take a week off next month?

good.english: We have a meeting that day, so it's hard.

items.english: Where are you going on your vacation?
distractors: When is your vacation?
Where did you go on vacation?
How long is your vacation?

good.english: I'm going to Jeju with my family.

items.english: Did you have a good vacation?
distractors: Are you going on vacation soon?
Have a good vacation.
Did you have a good business trip?

good.english: Yes, I had a good rest, thanks.

items.english: There's a team dinner this Friday.
items.note: 회식 is the team's dinner, usually with drinks. New staff are expected to come.
distractors: There was a team dinner last Friday.
This Friday's team dinner is cancelled.
There's a meeting this Friday.

good.english: Okay, what time does it start?

good.korean: 저는 그날 약속이 있어서 좀 늦을 것 같아요.
good.english: I have plans that day, so I'll be a bit late.

bad.english: Does this bus go to Seoul Station?

items.note: Saying so is fine. Hold out your glass for toasts and just take a sip, or drink a soft drink.
distractors: I drink quite a lot.
I don't like beer.
I can't eat spicy food.

good.english: That's fine, have a soft drink.

bad.english: Yes, two bottles of soju, please.

items.english: Let me pour you a glass.
items.note: Pour for seniors with both hands, and hold your glass with both hands when they pour for you.
distractors: Please pour me a glass.
Let me buy you a drink.
Let me get you a glass of water.

good.korean: 고마워요, 저도 한 잔 따라 드릴게요.
good.english: Thanks, I'll pour you one too.

items.english: to make a toast, to say cheers

items.note: The senior usually leads the toast. When clinking, juniors keep their glass a little lower.
distractors: Let's all go home together!
Let's all eat together!
Let's all take a photo together!

items.english: In front of seniors, you turn your head away to drink.
items.note: Turn slightly away and shield the glass with a hand when drinking with seniors.
distractors: In front of seniors, you drink looking straight at them.
In front of seniors, you pour your own drink.
In front of seniors, you don't drink at all.

items.english: Tonight's team dinner was really fun.
distractors: Tonight's team dinner was really boring.
Tomorrow's team dinner will be fun.
Today's meeting was really useful.

items.note: The boss often pays for 회식. Thank them like this, and again the next morning.
distractors: Enjoy your meal, director.
Dinner is on me, director.
Good night, director.
